overview.title: 📖 Overview: The Power of the Tongue
overview.subtitle: Arakhin 15a–15b
overview.hebrewSource: כׇּל הַמְסַפֵּר לָשׁוֹן הָרָע כְּאִילּוּ כָּפַר בָּעִיקָּר
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The daf finishes the mishna's treatment of a rapist and seducer, establishing through Abaye and Rava's readings of Deuteronomy 22:29 that the flat fifty-sela fine covers only the violation itself, leaving room for separately assessed payments for humiliation and degradation. A new mishna on a defamer, who falsely claims his bride was not a virgin, sets his fine at a flat one hundred sela — exactly double — from which the Gemara concludes that malicious speech is graver than a physical act, proven from the spies' evil report about the land, which alone sealed the decree that their generation would die in the wilderness. This launches an extended series of teachings, largely from Reish Lakish and Rabbi Yoḥanan in the name of Rabbi Yosei ben Zimra, on the severity of lashon hara: it is compared to denying God, it brings leprous marks, it kills at any distance like an arrow, it destroys three people at once, and the school of Rabbi Yishmael equates it with the three cardinal transgressions of idolatry, forbidden relations, and bloodshed combined.

slides.title: 💰 Why Doesn't the 50-Sela Fine Cover Everything?
slides.subtitle: Rav Zeira, Abaye, and Rava on humiliation and degradation

lines.speaker: Rav Zeira
lines.text: Had two men raped her — one atypically (leaving her technically intact) and one typically — would we really say both cases involve the same fifty-sela payment? That can't be the WHOLE story.

lines.speaker: Abaye
lines.text: By that logic, a healthy slave and one afflicted with boils should also differ in value — yet the ox's fine is a flat thirty sela regardless!

lines.speaker: Abaye's answer
lines.text: Rather: 'because he tormented her' (Deuteronomy 22:29) — the fifty sela covers only the ACT itself. Humiliation and degradation are separate, additional payments.

lines.speaker: Rava
lines.text: A parallel proof from 'lying with her': the fifty sela covers only the pleasure of the act, implying that something more — humiliation and degradation — is owed besides.

slides.title: 🗣️ New Mishna: The Defamer's Fine — Double the Rapist's
slides.subtitle: What the size of the fine reveals about speech versus action
rows: Fixed regardless of the victim's status (Deuteronomy 22:29)
Exactly DOUBLE the rapist's fine — 'one who speaks with his mouth is more severe than one who commits an act'

slides.title: 🕵️ Was It Really the Spies' Speech That Sealed the Decree?
slides.subtitle: Proving malicious speech, not accumulated sin, caused the harsh verdict

nodes.content: ❓ How do we know the decree that the wilderness generation would die there was sealed specifically for the spies' malicious report, rather than an accumulation of sins?

columns.label: Possible alternative
columns.content: Rav Hamnuna: God punishes only once a person's full measure of sin is reached — perhaps the report was merely the LAST straw

columns.label: Reish Lakish's proof
columns.content: The verse's extra word — 'they have tested Me THESE ten times' — pins the sealed decree to THIS specific sin, the report itself

nodes.content: 💡 Further objection: perhaps it was really their veiled BLASPHEMY ('stronger than Him') that was punished. Resolved: the verse says they died 'for bringing an evil report of the land' — pinning the punishment to the malicious speech itself

slides.title: ☠️ The Severity of Malicious Speech
slides.subtitle: A chain of teachings, mostly from Reish Lakish and Rabbi Yosei ben Zimra

steps.content: 1️⃣ The tongue is uniquely built for restraint — lying flat, hidden inside, walled by teeth and lips — yet still betrays; speaking lashon hara is like denying God entirely
2️⃣ Malicious speech brings leprous marks (tzara'at) — linked by a shared root, 'I will destroy him' (אַצְמִית) and 'in perpetuity' (לַצְּמִיתֻת)
3️⃣ It 'reaches the heavens' while the tongue 'walks the earth' — its harm has no distance limit, killing like an arrow, but from any range at all
4️⃣ 'Third-party speech kills three': the one who speaks it, the one who accepts it, and the one it is spoken about (a teaching from the Sages of the West)

slides.title: ⚖️ Malicious Speech vs. the Three Cardinal Sins
slides.subtitle: The school of Rabbi Yishmael's striking equation

boxes.title: Lashon Hara
items: The school of Rabbi Yishmael: equivalent to ALL THREE cardinal transgressions together, since none of the three could be singled out as lesser

boxes.title: The Three Cardinal Sins
items: Bloodshed — 'my sin is too great to bear' (Cain, Genesis 4:13)

callout.label: The remedy:
callout.text: A Torah scholar should immerse himself in Torah study; an unlearned person should cultivate humility — both practices diminish the impulse to speak maliciously.

summary.principle: A fixed monetary fine never captures the full weight of harm caused by an act — and the mishna's own numbers, comparing the rapist's fifty sela to the defamer's one hundred, become the springboard for the Gemara's extended teaching that malicious speech, though seemingly weightless, is judged more severely than almost any physical transgression.

flowSteps.content: 💰 The rapist/seducer's 50-sela fine covers only the act; humiliation and degradation are separately assessed
🗣️ New mishna: the defamer's fine is a flat 100 sela — double — proving speech outweighs action

columns.content: 🕵️ The spies' malicious report, not cumulative sin, sealed the decree — proven from 'these ten times'
☠️⚖️ Lashon hara brings tzara'at, kills at any distance, and equals the three cardinal sins combined

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: the tongue can do harm no fixed sum can measure — Torah study or humility are its only remedies

quiz.q: According to Abaye, what does the verse 'because he tormented her' (Deuteronomy 22:29) prove about the rapist or seducer's fifty-sela fine?
o: That the fine may be waived entirely under certain circumstances
That the fine covers only the act itself, implying separate additional payments exist for humiliation and degradation
That the fine applies only to seduction, not rape
That the fine must always equal one hundred sela
quiz.e: Abaye derives from this phrase that the fixed fifty-sela sum addresses only the torment of the act, leaving room for further, variable payments for humiliation and degradation.

quiz.q: According to the new mishna, how does the fine for a defamer (motzi shem ra) compare to that of a rapist or seducer?
o: It is exactly half as much
It is exactly the same amount
It is exactly double: 100 sela versus 50 sela
There is no fixed fine for a defamer
quiz.e: The mishna sets the defamer's fine at 100 sela, precisely double the rapist/seducer's 50 sela, from which the Gemara concludes that speech is judged more severely than action.

quiz.q: According to Reish Lakish, what proves that the harsh decree against the wilderness generation was sealed specifically because of the spies' malicious report, rather than an accumulation of unrelated sins?
o: A direct verse stating this explicitly with no ambiguity
The verse's extra word 'this' ('they have tested Me THESE ten times') pins the sealed decree to that specific sin
The fact that the spies were priests
There is no such proof; it remains a matter of speculation
quiz.e: Reish Lakish reads the extra word 'zeh' (this/these) in Numbers 14:22 as specifically identifying the spies' sin as the trigger for the sealed decree.

quiz.q: According to Rabbi Yochanan in the name of Rabbi Yosei ben Zimra, what physical affliction does one who speaks malicious speech bring upon himself?
o: Blindness
Leprous marks (tzara'at), derived from a shared root linking 'I will destroy him' to 'in perpetuity'
Deafness
Paralysis of the tongue
quiz.e: The Gemara links the verse 'whoever defames his neighbor in secret, I will destroy him' to the language used for tzara'at's permanent status, teaching that malicious speech brings leprous marks.

quiz.q: According to the school of Rabbi Yishmael, to how many of the three cardinal transgressions (idolatry, forbidden relations, bloodshed) is malicious speech equated?
o: Only idolatry
Two of the three
All three together, since the verse uses the plural 'great things' and none of the three could be excluded as lesser
None — the comparison is only rhetorical
quiz.e: The school of Rabbi Yishmael reasons that since malicious speech is described with the plural 'great things' and each cardinal sin is equally 'great,' none can be excluded — so it is equated with all three combined.
